messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Elevated crash rate detected in serving-runtime-prod (gpu-pool-west). Metric: container_restarts > baseline by 420% over 5m. Autoscale triggered.
ryan_oncall: on it. seeing repeated CrashLoopBackoff on pod model-serve-7f6c. Logs show CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS.
maya_engineering: can you paste the stack/log snippet?
ryan_oncall: here (truncated):
```
E tensorflow: 2026-03-15 02:21:14.123456 UTC - RuntimeError: Internal: CUDA error during kernel launch: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS (code=77)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  at runtime/loader.cu:0x7f8 - page_walk_handler +0x1f
  at runtime/infer.cu:0x2a - kv_cache_evict +0x3b
  at serving/main.cc:0x144 - dispatch_request
Kernel log: page_walk: invalid pte during pagewalk, addr=0x7ff3abcde000
```
alex_runtime: that page_walk line matches a race we saw in staging last month when concurrent_batching>1 + KV eviction overlapped with GPU page fault.
liz_sre: scope: how many nodes are affected?
ryan_oncall: 3/12 GPU nodes in west reported address faults and then kubelet restarted containers. other regions fine.
john_support: customer impact: two customers (acct-omega, acct-riverside) have 5xx rates ~18% and latency spikes. Support tickets incoming.
maya_engineering: immediate mitigation plan: 1) cordon affected nodes 2) reduce concurrency on rollout (set BATCH_SIZE=1) 3) enable fallback to cpu-variant for critical routes 4) roll out emergency patch to runtime to disable async prefetch.
alex_runtime: agree. also we should switch routing policy to prefer dedicated in other region for high-traffic customers while we investigate.
ryan_oncall: doing steps now. cordon nodes: `kubectl cordon gpu-west-02 gpu-west-05 gpu-west-11`
deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: Nodes cordoned (request by ryan_oncall).
ryan_oncall: reducing concurrency on model service for prod route `gen.v1.large`:
```
kubectl set env deploy/model-serve BATCH_SIZE=1 --namespace=prod
kubectl rollout restart deploy/model-serve --namespace=prod
```
ryan_oncall: restart done. observing fewer crashes on newly scheduled pods.
liz_sre: enabling cpu-fallback for top-5 routes via routing policy toggle in console.
maya_engineering: temporary runtime flag to disable async prefetch: `ENABLE_ASYNC_PREFETCH=false`. pushing patch to canary.
alex_runtime: can we get a core dump from one of the crashed pods for offline analysis? need `kubectl cp` and gcore.
ryan_oncall: capturing now: `gcloud compute ssh gpu-west-05 -- sudo journalctl -u kubelet -o cat | grep -A10 model-serve` then saving /mnt/ephemeral/dumps.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-20260315-0148 (sev=2). Pager: ryan_oncall. Timeline doc: https://internal.redwood/incedoc/INC-20260315-0148
john_support: I’ve opened customer tickets; letting them know we’ve initiated mitigations and may route their requests to CPU fallback with slight latency increase.
ryan_oncall: core dump obtained. uploading to s3: s3://redwood-incident-dumps/INC-20260315-0148/gpu-west-05-core.gz
maya_engineering: thanks. initial grep of core shows NV driver raising pagefault on invalid PTE during kernel memory copy. Not obvious yet whether driver or our kernel.
liz_sre: are there scheduled upgrades on these nodes (drivers/kernel)?
alex_runtime: nodes run driver 535.43, kernel 6.1.11-rt. Staging had driver 535.98 where we saw reduced repro.
maya_engineering: short-term: continue with BATCH_SIZE=1 and cpu-fallback for critical flows. mid-term: test 535.98 on a canary node.
ryan_oncall: can we spin up canary with driver 535.98 and runtime flag off?
alex_runtime: creating canary image with driver patch now. `gcloud instance-template create gpu-canary-53598 ...`
ryan_oncall: update monitoring dashboard to show crashrate by driver version.
incident-bot: Note: Auto-scaling policy has been paused for this pool (action by liz_sre).
john_support: customers notified: acct-omega updated (ticket #12345). They report degraded throughput but accepts fallback.
maya_engineering: root-cause hypothesis: a rare race in our GPU kernel path where concurrent KV eviction triggers an orphaned pagewalk -> driver raises CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS -> kernel OOM/abort path causes container crash. repro requires high concurrency + eviction window.
liz_sre: next steps owner: maya_engineering for root cause & patch. timeframe: hotfix in 6 hrs to disable async prefetch by default; long fix (kernel guard) tracked in ENG-REPRO-642.
ryan_oncall: on-call handoff: I will stay until stabilization, then hand to liz at 06:00 UTC.
alex_runtime: patches to test: 1) driver 535.98 on canary 2) runtime patch to serialize KV eviction 3) backoff batcher to avoid concurrent eviction.
maya_engineering: I pushed canary runtime with ENABLE_ASYNC_PREFETCH=false to gpu-canary-01. No crashes after 20m.
ryan_oncall: Observed 90% drop in crash metric on patched canary vs baseline.
john_support: updating customers: will keep them posted every 30 minutes.
liz_sre: ops checklist for recovery: - keep nodes cordoned until we validate driver patch - gradually uncordon one node at a time after driver update - run load for 1h with BATCH_SIZE=1 - remove cpu-fallback after 2h stable - prepare rollback steps if crash rate increases
maya_engineering: forensics: attaching snippet of suspicious log pattern: `kv_evict_async: seq=0x3f9 flags=0x2 attempt=4 -> page_walk_start(addr=0x7ff3abcde000) -> driver: pagefault during mmio`
alex_runtime: I also captured a brief perf trace showing overlapping `evict_kv` and `prefetch_async` on same GPU context. Will upload to traces: https://internal.redwood/traces/INC-20260315-0148/trace001
ryan_oncall: summary for postmortem: - symptom: GPU containers crash with CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS during high-concurrency infer workloads - impact: 2 paying customers degraded, 3 GPU nodes cordoned - mitigations: BATCH_SIZE=1, cpu-fallback routing, cordon nodes, canary runtime with async prefetch disabled - next: driver upgrade trial, serialized eviction patch, tracking ENG-REPRO-642
john_support: logging incident notes to customer tickets and CS Slack channel.
incident-bot: Auto-reminder: Please file postmortem draft within 48h. Assigned: maya_engineering, reviewer: liz_sre.
ryan_oncall: handing off to liz_sre at 06:00 UTC. I’m marking the thread for follow-up. :thumbsup:
liz_sre: taking over. keeping watch and coordinating driver canary.
maya_engineering: I'll start the postmortem doc and include repro steps, logs, and mitigations.
alex_runtime: once we validate driver canary, propose schedule to upgrade remaining nodes with rolling reboot and health checks.
john_support: will keep customers in the loop.
liz_sre: closing note: sev downgraded to sev-3 (partial impact) after mitigations reduced crash rate. Will update timeline when fully resolved.
